title: Rostam and Sohrab
text:
The great hero Rostam, hunting near the borders of Turan, lost his horse Rakhsh and followed its tracks to the city of Samangan. There he spent a night with Tahmineh, the king's daughter, and they married. In the morning he left, giving her a token to fasten on the arm of their child, if a child came.

A son was born, Sohrab. He grew quickly into a young warrior of extraordinary strength. When his mother told him who his father was, he decided to lead an army into Iran, overthrow its king and place Rostam on the throne. The ruler of Turan, Afrasiab, eager to set father and son against each other, gave him troops and saw to it that he would not learn which of the Iranian champions was Rostam.

So the two met on the battlefield as strangers. Sohrab sensed something and asked his opponent directly whether he was Rostam. Rostam denied it. They fought for days. Sohrab threw Rostam once and spared him; on the next day Rostam threw Sohrab and drove his dagger into his chest.

Dying, Sohrab warned that his father Rostam would avenge him. Rostam tore open his armor and saw the token on his arm. He begged the king for a healing potion, but it came too late. Sohrab died in his father's arms.
lesson: Distance and pride can make family members strangers to each other. Ask the direct question, and answer it honestly, before it is too late.
people: Rostam, Sohrab, Tahmineh, Afrasiab, Kay Kavus
location: Persia (Iran and Turan, ancient epic geography)
source: Ferdowsi, Shahnameh, the story of Rostam and Sohrab
